title.en: Middle East crisis live: Jordan says it foiled Iranian missile attack as US launches ‘heavy’ strikes on Iran after pause
title.zh: 中东危机：美国在暂停数日后对伊朗发动新一轮袭击

summary.en: The United States has launched fresh strikes on Iran, following a brief pause in attacks. Analysts warn that these reciprocal military actions by both sides significantly increase the risk of a return to all-out war, pushing the region into uncharted territory.
summary.zh: 在短暂暂停袭击后，美国对伊朗发动了新一轮打击。分析人士警告称，双方的这些军事行动大大增加了全面战争再次爆发的风险，将该地区推向“未知领域”。

body.en: Jordanian military says it intercepted five missiles targeting the kingdom after US military says it hit dozens of Revolutionary Guard targets on Thursday US launches fresh strikes on Iran after days-long pause, amid fears the war is widening A liquefied natural gas tanker controlled by QatarEnergy exited the strait of Hormuz overnight – the first such vessel ⁠visible on ship-tracking data to ⁠leave the waterway ​since 11 July, data from analytics firms showed on Thursday. The Al Areesh tanker , which loaded a cargo at Qatar’s Ras Laffan terminal around 4-6 July, sailed ⁠out of the strait overnight on 29 July, according to Kpler and LSEG data. Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国周四早些时候宣布发动袭击，专家表示，双方前一天进行的袭击增加了全面战争爆发的风险。分析人士警告称，美国和沙特对伊拉克的袭击将地区推向“未知领域”。伊朗半官方通讯社塔斯尼姆通讯社称，伊朗格什姆岛发生三起爆炸。霍尔木兹海峡附近的海湾岛屿是伊朗攻击艇、无人机、水雷和其他用于破坏重要能源路线运输的材料的储存地点。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The escalating military actions between nations remind us of the ancient warning that those who live by the sword often perish by it. This cycle of retaliation, where each strike invites another, only deepens conflict and moves further from peace. May leaders seek paths that break this destructive pattern, for the sake of all involved.
reflection.zh: 国家之间不断升级的军事行动提醒我们，古老的警告是，那些靠刀剑而活的人，也必死于刀剑之下。这种以牙还牙的报复循环，只会加深冲突，使和平之路更加遥远。愿领袖们为所有相关者的福祉，寻求打破这种破坏性模式的道路。

verse.textEn: All who draw the sword will die by the sword.
verse.textZh: 凡动刀的，必死在刀下。

Yahweh's word affirms that a leader's authority is strengthened when wrongdoing is detested and...

title.en: Firefighters race to extinguish blazes across EU as fire weather breaks records
title.zh: 消防员在欧盟各地扑灭大火，火灾天气打破纪录

summary.en: European Forest Fire Information Service data indicates that fire weather conditions across the EU are 43% more severe than the average for the same period over the last two decades, with firefighters actively working to control numerous blazes.
summary.zh: 欧洲森林火灾信息服务中心的数据显示，欧盟的火灾天气状况比过去20年同期平均水平严重43%，消防员正全力扑灭多处火灾。

body.en: European Forest Fire Information Service figures show conditions in EU 43% more severe than for same period in last 20 years Fire weather in the EU has broken records for severity for this time of year, new data shows, as firefighters race to extinguish blazes across the Mediterranean. Inflamed by carbon pollution, the hot, dry and windy weather across the EU since the start of the year has been 43% more severe than the end-of-July average over the last two decades, data from the European Forest Fire Information Service (Effis) shows. Continue reading...
body.zh: 欧洲森林火灾信息服务机构的数据显示，欧盟的情况比过去20年同期严重43%。新数据显示，随着消防员竞相扑灭地中海大火，欧盟的火灾天气打破了每年这个时候的严重程度记录。欧洲森林火灾信息服务处 (Effis) 的数据显示，受碳污染影响，今年以来欧盟各地炎热、干燥和多风的天气比过去二十年七月底的平均水平严重了 43%。继续阅读...

As firefighters bravely battle these blazes, we are called to reflect on our role in stewarding the earth and the impact of our actions on the natural world. This ongoing struggle highlights the deep connection between...

body.en: With his popularity at historic lows, Friedrich Merz seeks spiritual guidance from Pope Leo’s encyclical on AI Europe live – latest updates Summer is normally thought of as the time for pacy potboilers and brain-soothing pageturners – airport reads that wind up sandy and sunscreen-stained. Not so for Friedrich Merz ’s holiday reading list. Germany ’s embattled chancellor, who has faced one rough patch after another since taking office 14 months ago, seems to be seeking spiritual guidance this year while putting his feet up. Continue reading...

reflection.zh: 面对公众审视和人工智能等复杂议题，一位领导人选择寻求属灵指引，反映了人类在传统政治之外对智慧的深切需求。雅伟应许慷慨地赐予智慧给那些求问祂的人，在充满挑战的时刻带来清晰和洞察。

title.en: Missile that left crater deep inside Poland was probably Russian - Polish PM
title.zh: 波兰总理：在波兰深处留下弹坑的导弹可能是俄罗斯制造的

summary.en: The missile left a 10m-wide (33ft) crater a short distance from the village of Tarnawa Kolonia, about 100km from the border with Ukraine.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has said an object that crashed into a field in eastern Poland in the early hours of Thursday was probably a Russian missile.

The unidentified object caused a 10m-wide (33ft) crater a short distance from the village of Tarnawa Kolonia, about 100km (62 miles) from the border with Ukraine during a large-scale Russian attack on the cities of Lviv, Kyiv and near Kryvyhi Rih.

Tusk said initially that "all the indications" were that the missile that violated Polish airspace was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile, during a specially convened meeting in the eastern city of Lublin.

He then went to the site of the incident and said that according to military experts the majority of "recovered fragments point to it being a Russian Kh-101 missile".

Although no casualties had been reported in Thursday's incident near Tarnawa Kolonia, the Polish prime minister made clear it was being taken very seriously.

There was no immediate threat as it had not landed in a built-up area, he said, adding that "we were prepared to shoot it down if had continued its flight".

Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said about 20 objects were seen close to Polish airspace overnight and pyrotechnical analysis was being carried out.

Ukraine's acting Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha had earlier declared definitively that a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile had "crossed into Poland as part of Russia's massive strike against Ukraine, violating Nato airspace".

Tusk said he was in contact with fellow European leaders and the head of the European Council António Costa said Russia's "massive combined strike against Ukraine" had underlined again that "Russia's aggression is a threat to the security as a whole".

At least eight people died and dozens more were wounded across Ukraine, including six members of one family in a village near Kryvyih Rih. Dozens more were wounded in Lviv, not far from Ukraine's western border with Poland.

A number of Russian drones and one unarmed Russian missile have landed in Poland since Russia's full-scale war in Ukraine began in February 2022.

Two Polish farmers were killed by a missile that landed just over the border from Ukraine in November 2022, but that was believed to have been a Ukrainian air defence missile responding to a Russian attack.

Poland's military detected the object at about 03:40 on Thursday (01:40 GMT) and sent an F-16 fighter jet to intercept it before it disappeared minutes later from radar systems. A military helicopter was then sent to search the area.

body.zh: 波兰总理唐纳德·图斯克表示，周四凌晨坠入波兰东部田野的一个物体可能是一枚俄罗斯导弹。 在俄罗斯对利沃夫、基辅和克利维希里赫附近城市进行大规模袭击时，这个不明物体在距离乌克兰边境约 100 公里（62 英里）的 Tarnawa Kolonia 村附近造成了一个 10m 宽（33 英尺）的弹坑。 图斯克在东部城市卢布林举行的一次特别会议上最初表示，“所有迹象”都表明，侵犯波兰领空的导弹是俄罗斯 Kh-101 巡航导弹。 随后他前往事发地点并表示，根据军事专家的说法，大多数“回收的碎片表明这是一枚俄罗斯 Kh-101 导弹”。 尽管周四塔尔纳瓦科洛尼亚附近的事件没有造成人员伤亡，但波兰总理明确表示正在非常严肃地对待这起事件。 他说，由于它没有降落在建筑区，所以没有立即构成威胁，并补充说，“如果它继续飞行，我们准备将其击落”。 波兰国防部长瓦迪斯瓦夫·科西尼亚克-卡米什表示，夜间在波兰领空附近发现了约20个物体，目前正在进行烟火分析。 乌克兰代理外交部长安德烈·西比哈早些时候明确宣布，一枚俄罗斯Kh-101巡航导弹“作为俄罗斯对乌克兰大规模打击的一部分进入波兰，侵犯了北约领空”。 图斯克表示，他正在与其他欧洲领导人保持联系，欧洲理事会主席安东尼奥·科斯塔表示，俄罗斯“对乌克兰的大规模联合打击”再次强调“俄罗斯的侵略是对整个安全的威胁”。 乌克兰各地至少有八人死亡，数十人受伤，其中包括克里沃罗格附近一个村庄的一个家庭的六名成员。利沃夫距离乌克兰西部与波兰边境不远，另有数十人受伤。 自 2022 年 2 月俄罗斯在乌克兰全面战争开始以来，多架俄罗斯无人机和一枚非武装俄罗斯导弹已降落在波兰。 2022 年 11 月，一枚导弹落在乌克兰边境上空，两名波兰农民被炸死，但据信那是乌克兰防空导弹对俄罗斯袭击的回应。 波兰军方于周四凌晨 3 点 40 分（格林威治标准时间 01 点 40 分）左右发现了该物体，并派出一架 F-16 战斗机进行拦截，几分钟后该物体从雷达系统中消失。随后派出一架军用直升机前往该地区进行搜索。 由于俄罗斯对邻国乌克兰的空袭，东南部的卢布林和克拉斯尼斯塔夫拉响了空袭警报。 Tarnawa Kolonia 的居民报告称，凌晨 04:00 左右听到一声巨响，警方找到了坠机地点……

title.en: US launches 'heavy' strikes on Iran after attempted attack on American troops
title.zh: 美国在美军遇袭后对伊朗发动“猛烈”打击

summary.en: The US military launched strikes against Iran, stating they were in response to Iran's missile attacks on US forces in the Middle East earlier in the week.
summary.zh: 美国军方对伊朗发动了袭击，称此举是对伊朗本周早些时候向中东美军发射导弹的回应。

body.en:
The US military says it has completed a "heavy wave" of strikes against Iran in retaliation for Tuesday's attempted ballistic missile attacks on American forces.

Centcom said it hit "dozens" of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in response to Iran's firing on US bases in Jordan and at ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian state media said the latest strikes had killed three people, including a two-year-old child, on Qeshm island, while other locations were also hit in the south and west of the country.

The latest hostilities come on a week that has seen the conflict expand, with the first publicly announced joint US-Saudi strikes targeting Iranian proxies in Iraq.

Iran and the US have engaged in escalating strikes and counter-strikes since a ceasefire in April, aimed at pausing the months-long war, fell apart in June.

The US has blockaded Iranian ports and bombed Iranian sites, while Iran has fired missiles and drones at US assets in countries across the Middle East and targeted shipping in the economically important Strait of Hormuz, connecting the Gulf and Arabian Sea.

On Wednesday, news outlet Axios cited an unnamed US official as saying that Trump had met Saudi defence minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, who had conveyed that Saudi Arabia wants to de-escalate tensions. The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.

Meanwhile, the Egyptian government said a fire at a port on Wednesday had been caused by a drone attack. Egypt, a US ally, has not previously been directly attacked during the war.

For days, both sides halted strikes as talks apparently restarted in hopes of some type of diplomatic solution. Trump called them "very friendly negotiations", though Tehran denied any discussions were happening.

But following the Iranian missile attack on a US base in Jordan on Tuesday, Trump vowed to retaliate, telling reporters at the White House: "We're going to be hitting them very hard because it's our turn to hit them. They know it's coming. They asked us not to do it."

title.en: Nicaraguan leader proposes extending presidential term by another year
title.zh: 尼加拉瓜领导人提议将总统任期再延长一年

summary.en: Nicaragua's 80-year-old leader, Daniel Ortega, has proposed another extension to his presidential term. This marks multiple instances where the constitution has been altered to allow him to remain in power.
summary.zh: 尼加拉瓜80岁的领导人丹尼尔·奥尔特加提议再次延长其总统任期。这已是多次修改宪法以允许他继续掌权。

body.en:
Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega, who has been in power since 2007, has proposed extending the presidential term by another year.

The government-controlled National Assembly is expected to approve the extension in September.

It is part of a proposed constitutional reform which also includes plans to bar members of the opposition deemed by the government to be "traitors" or "coup plotters" from running for office.

The 80-year-old's rule has become increasingly authoritarian, with political opponents jailed, sent into exile and stripped of their citizenship.

During Ortega's 19 years in power, there have been several changes to the presidential term already.

In 2014, the country's National Assembly scrapped presidential term limits and in 2024 it extended the term from five to six years.

The legislative body also approved Ortega's plan to name his wife, Rosario Murillo, as "co-president".

It thereby paved the way for her to assume as president should Ortega, who is believed to be in frail health, be declared "permanently absent".

The one-sided contest was won by Ortega following a brutal crackdown on the opposition.

Any rival potential candidates with a chance to garner a significant number of votes were detained and disqualified from standing for office or forced into exile. Dozens of other opposition members were also arrested.

Only a small handful of little-known candidates, who were unlikely to get much support, were allowed to stand.

United Nations human rights chief Volker Türk has warned that government repression has deepened further since then, with the rule of law steadily eroded and the persecution of political dissidents escalating.

Few Nicaraguans have dared to speak out in public against Ortega and Murillo since more than 300 people were killed when the security forces quashed anti-government protests in 2018.

Dissidents living in exile have also been targeted with many stripped of their citizenship by the Ortega government, their homes they left behind in Nicaragua seized and sold.
body.zh: 自2007年开始执政的尼加拉瓜总统丹尼尔·奥尔特加提议将总统任期再延长一年。 政府控制的国民议会预计将在 9 月批准延期。 这是拟议宪法改革的一部分，其中还包括禁止被政府视为“叛徒”或“政变策划者”的反对派成员竞选公职的计划。 这位80岁老人的统治变得越来越独裁，政治对手被监禁、流放并被剥夺公民身份。 奥尔特加执政19年期间，总统任期已发生数次变动。 2014年，该国国民议会取消了总统任期限制，并于2024年将总统任期从五年延长至六年。 立法机构还批准了奥尔特加任命其妻子罗萨里奥·穆里略为“联合总统”的计划。 因此，如果据信健康状况不佳的奥尔特加被宣布“永久缺席”，这将为她担任总统铺平道路。 奥尔特加在残酷镇压反对派后赢得了这场一边倒的比赛。 任何有机会获得大量选票的竞争对手的潜在候选人都会被拘留，并被取消竞选公职的资格或被迫流亡。数十名其他反对派成员也被捕。 只有少数鲜为人知且不太可能获得太多支持的候选人被允许参选。 联合国人权事务高级专员沃尔克·蒂尔克警告说，自那时以来，政府的镇压进一步加深，法治不断受到侵蚀，对政治异见人士的迫害不断升级。 自 2018 年安全部队镇压反政府抗议活动导致 300 多人死亡以来，很少有尼加拉瓜人敢于公开反对奥尔特加和穆里略。 流亡海外的持不同政见者也成为奥尔特加政府的目标，许多人被剥夺了公民身份，他们留在尼加拉瓜的房屋被没收和出售。

title.en: Crete wildfires cause evacuations and firefighter deaths
title.zh: 克里特岛野火导致疏散和消防员死亡

summary.en: Wildfires on the Greek island of Crete are forcing thousands of residents and tourists to evacuate. Three firefighters have died as Greece becomes the latest country, after France and Spain, to face summer blazes.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Wildfires on the Greek island of Crete are forcing thousands of residents and tourists to evacuate. Three firefighters have died as Greece becomes the latest country, after France and Spain, to face summer blazes.

Greek firefighters battled deadly wildfires on the island of Crete for a second day on Thursday as strong winds made it difficult to contain the flames.

Two firefighters were killed while responding to fires on the island, while a third died fighting a separate blaze on the Greek mainland.

Fires advancing across southwestern Crete forced several villages in the Rethymno region to be evacuated. Flames also neared the popular resort town of Agia Galini on the island's southern coast, pushing tourists to leave. 

In total, roughly 8,000 people were evacuated, the island's deputy governor Maria Lioni said.

The fires have already destroyed large areas of farmland, including olive groves, as well as residential homes.

Firefighters have struggled to contain the blazes because of strong and constantly shifting winds, which have reached speeds of up to 102 kilometers (63 miles) per hour.

As a result, emergency services said aircraft used to drop water on the fires were severely limited or could not be deployed at all.

"Unfortunately there is no improvement, and the latest information ​indicates that winds will increase later in the day," Giorgos Tsapakos, the deputy regional governor for civil protection on Crete, told Greek television.

Two firefighters died combating the flames in Crete after being trapped on a mountain road, losing their bearings as smoke enveloped them. A third firefighter collapsed and died while on duty near Gytheio on the Southern end of the Peloponnese peninsula.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis paid tribute to the fallen firefighters on Wednesday, acknowledging the "new harsh reality” they face each year, as wildfires worsen. 

Greece , like other Southern European countries, is facing a heightened risk of wildfires as climate change exacerbates droughts, high temperatures and extreme winds  which create ideal conditions for blazes.

In France and Spain, meanwhile, firefighting efforts on Thursday seemed to be turning a corner.

In France, authorities permitted the return of 84,000 evacuees forced out by a wildfire near the southwestern city of Bordeaux, as cooler temperatures and rain offered some respite. The fire had led to around 220,000 people being displaced .

In Spain, too, wildfires threatening Madrid were abating, as authorities reported "almost no flames" left.

title.en: Veteran Ugandan opposition leader collapses in court and in ICU, his wife says
title.zh: 乌干达资深反对派领导人在法庭上晕倒，妻子称其已送入重症监护室

summary.en: A 70-year-old veteran opposition leader in Uganda, detained since November 2024 and facing treason charges he denies, collapsed in court and has been admitted to the ICU, according to his wife.
summary.zh: 乌干达一位70岁的资深反对派领导人自2024年11月以来一直被拘留，面临叛国罪指控，但他否认这些指控。据其妻子称，他近日在法庭上晕倒，已被送入重症监护室。

body.en:
Ugandan opposition leader Kizza Besigye has been admitted to an intensive care unit (ICU) in the capital, Kampala, after collapsing and losing consciousness during his treason trial, his wife has said.

The 70-year-old has been in detention since November 2024. His lead lawyer was arrested last month and charged with allegedly failing to report acts of treason .

The visibly frail politician was objecting to state lawyers being appointed to represent him when he fell, prompting prison guards to rush him to hospital.

"He is unconscious, unable to speak, and unresponsive even to a pain stimulus," his wife, Winnie Byanyima, who heads the UN's agency tackling HIV and Aids (UNAids), wrote on X.

Besigye, who has run for president against long-serving leader Yoweri Museveni four times, was dramatically abducted in Kenya in 2024 and taken back to Uganda.

He has since been held along with his aide, Obeid Lutale, and both have been charged with treason, which they deny.

Prosecutors allege that Besigye and his co-accused plotted to overthrow President Museveni's government.

Treason is a capital offence in Uganda and if found guilty the veteran politician could be sentenced to death.

During Wednesday's hearing at the High Court in Kampala witnesses in court said Besigye repeatedly shouted "stop" about his legal representation before collapsing.

"Before he collapsed, he cried out that he was being injured," his wife posted, adding that Besigye's sister Olive Kobusingye, who is a doctor, was in court but was not allowed to attend to him.

He was transferred to Mulago National Referral Hospital, Uganda's largest public hospital, but was refusing treatment from government medical personnel.

His wife demanded that Besigye be allowed to receive treatment from his personal physician at a private clinic rather than at a government health facility.

The ICU wing where Besigye is being treated is guarded by heavily armed security officers. Reports say his sister, who is also his personal doctor, has now been allowed to see him.

Besigye's main lawyer, Erias Lukwago, is in jail after being seized by the army last month.

His other lead lawyer, prominent Kenyan Martha Karua, was then barred from entering the country when she flew in to represent him last month .

There have been increasing calls by the family, opposition and human rights groups for Besigye to be released on medical grounds.

On Wednesday, Besigye's son, Adam Ampa, appealed to President Museveni and his son, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is Uganda's army chief, to show mercy by releasing his father on humanitarian grounds.

"Regardless of politics, no son should have to witness his father reach such a state while standing before the very law he served and dedicated his life," Ampa wrote in an open...
body.zh: 乌干达反对派领导人基扎·贝西杰的妻子表示，他在叛国罪审判期间昏倒并失去知觉，目前已被送进首都坎帕拉的重症监护室（ICU）。 这位 70 岁的老人自 2024 年 11 月以来一直被拘留。他的首席律师上个月被捕，并被指控涉嫌未报告叛国行为。 这位明显虚弱的政客在摔倒时反对任命州律师代表他，促使狱警将他送往医院。 “他失去知觉，无法说话，甚至对疼痛刺激也没有反应，”他的妻子、联合国艾滋病毒和艾滋病机构（UNAids）负责人温妮·拜安伊玛（Winnie Byanyima）在 X 上写道。 贝西杰曾四次竞选总统，与长期任职的领导人约韦里·穆塞韦尼 (Yoweri Museveni) 竞争，他于 2024 年在肯尼亚戏剧性地被绑架并被带回乌干达。 此后，他和他的助手奥贝德·卢塔莱 (Obeid Lutale) 一起被关押，两人都被指控犯有叛国罪，但他们否认了这一点。 检察官指控贝西杰和他的同案被告密谋推翻穆塞韦尼总统的政府。 叛国罪在乌干达是一种死罪，如果罪名成立，这位资深政客可能会被判处死刑。 周三在坎帕拉高等法院举行的听证会上，法庭上的目击者表示，贝西杰在倒下之前多次对他的律师代表大喊“停止”。 “在他倒下之前，他大喊自己受伤了，”他的妻子发帖说，并补充说贝西杰的妹妹奥利弗·科布辛耶是一名医生，她当时在法庭上，但不被允许照顾他。 他被转移到乌干达最大的公立医院穆拉戈国家转诊医院，但拒绝政府医务人员的治疗。 他的妻子要求允许贝西杰在私人诊所而不是政府医疗机构接受私人医生的治疗。 贝西杰接受治疗的重症监护病房由全副武装的保安人员把守。报道称，他的妹妹，也是他的私人医生，现已获准见他。 贝西杰的主要律师埃里亚斯·卢克瓦戈(Erias Lukwago)上个月被军队抓获后入狱。 他的另一位首席律师、著名的肯尼亚人玛莎·卡鲁亚(Martha Karua)上个月飞来代表他时被禁止入境。 贝西杰的家人、反对派和人权组织越来越多地呼吁以健康为由释放贝西杰。 周三，贝西杰的儿子亚当·安帕呼吁穆塞韦尼总统和他的儿子、乌干达陆军参谋长穆胡齐·凯内鲁加巴将军以人道主义为由释放他的父亲。 安帕在公开信中写道：“无论政治如何，任何儿子都不应该在站在他所服务并奉献一生的法律面前目睹他的父亲达到这样的境界。”

reflection.en: This verse reminds us of the profound impact leaders have on the well-being of their citizens. When those in power act with cruelty or injustice, the people, especially those who challenge the status quo, can face immense suffering and vulnerability. It calls us to pray for leaders who govern with compassion and righteousness, protecting all their people.

title.en: French student fined over Singapore straw licking prank
title.zh: 法国学生因新加坡舔吸管恶作剧被罚款

summary.en: A French student faces a substantial fine and potential deportation from Singapore after a social media prank involving licking a straw went viral.
summary.zh: 一名法国学生因在社交媒体上发布舔吸管的恶作剧视频而面临巨额罚款，并可能影响其在新加坡的居留权。

body.en:
A social media stunt involving a single straw has left a French student facing a hefty fine — and possible consequences for his right to remain in Singapore.

A French student has been fined 600 Singapore dollars (€400, $458) after licking a drinking straw and returning it to a dispenser in a prank filmed for social media.

The 19-year-old, Didier Gaspard Owen Maximilien, pleaded guilty to a public nuisance charge.

He avoided a possible prison sentence, but it remains unclear whether authorities will revoke his student pass. The French national studies at Singapore's ESSEC Business School.

Maximilien removed a straw from a freshly squeezed orange juice vending machine in March, licked it and placed it back in the dispenser.

An employee of the company operating the machine saw the footage and contacted police. As a result, all 500 straws in the dispenser had to be replaced.

The direct cost amounted to just 5 Singapore dollars, or around €3.30, according to court documents, but the case attracted nationwide attention.

Maximilien could have faced several months in prison, a fine, or both after being convicted of disturbing public order.

His lawyer told the court that he was remorseful and now understood that an apparently harmless prank could have far-reaching consequences.

The wealthy city-state is known for its strict laws and rigorous enforcement, with cleanliness and tightly regulated public spaces forming part of its image for decades.

The import of chewing gum, for example, remains largely prohibited as part of efforts to prevent littering and vandalism.

Singapore also retains judicial caning for certain serious offenses, although the punishment was not applicable in the student's case.

Just as a tiny spark can set a large forest ablaze, our actions, especially online, can have far-reaching and unintended consequences. title.en: As eSafety takes Telegram to court, Russia moves against the man behind the app
title.zh: eSafety 将 Telegram 告上法庭，俄罗斯对该应用程序背后的人采取行动

summary.en: Australia and Russia both cited terrorism concerns, though for very different reasons.

body.en:
Australia's eSafety Commissioner has announced legal action against messaging app Telegram for its failure to remove terrorist content, just one day after Russia charged the app's founder with aiding Ukrainian spies to co-ordinate domestic terrorist attacks.

eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant told reporters on Thursday that Telegram continued to host videos linked to the Christchurch mosque shootings and executions by the self-proclaimed Islamic State group, both illegal and restricted Class 1 content in Australia.

Grant said the app has "a fundamental responsibility to take reasonable steps to prevent the hosting, sharing and amplification of this harmful material".

Telegram, based in the United Arab Emirates, is one of the world's largest messaging platforms with more than one billion active users worldwide. It is not included in Australia's youth social media ban .

Grant said her agency first began compliance talks with the digital platform in March 2024. Despite Telegram's engagement, Grant said the platform continued to host harmful content.

"We allege that this content remained publicly accessible on the service long after Telegram had been put on notice by user reports," she said.

The maximum penalty for non-compliance is $54.4 million; however, Grant told the press that the appropriate penalty was a "matter for the court".

In 2025, Telegram was fined $957,780 by the eSafety Commissioner for delays in reporting the steps the platform has taken to minimise terrorism and child abuse material.

On Wednesday, Russia said it had charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activity, alleging the app was being used by Ukrainian spies to organise attacks inside Russia.

In response, Telegram's official account on X posted an image of the Russian-born billionaire making an obscene gesture with his middle finger.

The charges, announced by Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB), marked the culmination of a long investigation against Dubai-based Durov and Telegram.

Russia has effectively throttled the service as part of a wider campaign to cut off access to foreign tech platforms and tighten control over the internet.

Russians can now access Telegram only via a virtual private network to encrypt traffic and conceal their location. Yet state bodies including the Kremlin and the defence ministry continue to post to it daily.

The app has been described as a "virtual battlefield" in the war between Russia and Ukraine, where it is used by officials, soldiers and influential bloggers on both sides.

title.en: Japan's urgent search for mall collapse survivors as earthquake death toll rises to 17
title.zh: 日本地震造成13人死亡，紧急搜寻购物中心倒塌幸存者

summary.en: Rescuers are urgently searching for survivors in the wreckage of an Aeon Mall complex that collapsed during an earthquake in Japan, where the death toll currently stands at 13.
summary.zh: 日本发生地震，一座永旺购物中心倒塌，造成13人死亡，救援人员正在紧急搜寻幸存者。

body.en:
At least 17 people have died after a major earthquake struck Japan, local authorities said on Thursday in a revised toll two days after the tremor.

The Kumamoto disaster management office's latest tally put fatalities at 17 and the number of those without vital signs at six, with five more in critical condition.

Rescuers have continued to battle through the tangled wreckage of a Japanese shopping mall searching for any trapped survivors.

A massive explosion ripped through the mall around 50 minutes after the 7.1-magnitude tremor on Tuesday in the southwestern Kumamoto region, where in 2016 twin quakes killed nearly 300 people.

The earthquake caused widespread damage on the island of Kyushu, flattening homes, triggering fires and leaving tens of thousands of residents without power and water.

Akio Yoshida, the president of mall operator Aeon, said three people died at the facility in the town of Kashima, with one more fatality feared and three others missing.

"The cause is still being investigated, but it's likely that gas caused it," fellow Aeon executive Keiji Ohno told a news conference where he and others bowed in apology.

Five people were also confirmed killed, and four others were unaccounted for at the Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro city, where part of a red-and-white smokestack collapsed, a government official told reporters from the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency.

Government spokesman Minoru Kihara said that as of early Wednesday, more than 9,000 people had sought refuge in 506 shelters across three regions of Kyushu Island.

Around 130 police, 450 firefighters and 170 military personnel were involved in the rescue operation at the Aeon Mall Kumamoto, he said.

Some stunned locals said the quake was the biggest they had felt in their lifetimes, measuring at the top of Japan's seven-level shindo scale of shakiness.

"It was the strongest quake I ever experienced," Kanzo Matsumoto, 73, the operator of a luxury onsen hot spring inn in Yatsushiro, told AFP.

Japan's Geospatial Information Authority said some ground surfaces were displaced by up to 87 centimetres during the quake, Jiji Press reported.

Tokito Kitagawa, 21, pulled over at a convenience store when the quake struck as he was travelling in Kumamoto on his motorcycle.

"There was a sudden big noise," Kitagawa told AFP. "I couldn't stay standing. I had to crouch down. Then all the cup noodles fell all over me on the floor."

One user on X who said that they worked inside the mall recounted the moments after the quake hit.

title.en: Massive strikes launched on Ukraine as Poland claims to have been hit by Russian missile
title.zh: 泽连斯基在炼油厂遇袭后，呼吁乌克兰人做好准备应对“大规模”俄罗斯袭击

summary.en: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has urged his nation to prepare for a significant Russian attack, following recent strikes on oil refineries. This development occurs amidst ongoing conflict with Russia and a reportedly improving relationship between Zelenskyy and Donald Trump.
summary.zh: 乌克兰总统泽连斯基在炼油厂遭到袭击后，敦促全国人民为俄罗斯的大规模袭击做好准备。这一事态发展正值乌克兰与俄罗斯的持续冲突以及泽连斯基与唐纳德·特朗普关系据报回暖之际。

body.en:
Russian strikes killed at least eight people and wounded more than a dozen others across Ukraine, authorities said on Thursday, triggering renewed calls from Kyiv for its allies to send air defence supplies.

The attack involved 74 missiles and 284 drones, according to the Ukrainian air force, and resulted in casualties in the capital Kyiv, the central city of Kryvyi Rig, and in Poltava.

Russia's defence ministry said it had hit Ukrainian military-industrial complex, military communications, and logistics centres. It claimed to have hit the western city of Lviv, and had struck three cargo ships in the Black Sea.

Ukraine's air force said it managed to intercept 55 missiles and 265 drones launched by Moscow.

In neighbouring Poland, a European Union and NATO member, fighter jets were scrambled to secure airspace during the attack.

A 10-metre-wide crater in a field was discovered, believed to have been caused by a Russian missile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Thursday.

"All the indications are that it was a Russian Kh-101 ballistic missile, but we want to be 100% certain about the type of missile and who launched it," Tusk told an emergency meeting.

Russian drones have previously been detected flying through Polish airspace during attacks, while in 2022 two people in a border village were killed by a misfiring Ukrainian air defence missile.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy refreshed his call for more air defence supplies to protect Ukraine against Russia's ballistic missiles.

"Given the critical shortage of air defense missiles from our partners, our warriors are accomplishing truly incredible things," Zelenskyy said.

The Ukrainian leader on Tuesday had discussed anti-ballistic defence with his United States counterpart Donald Trump at the White House and discussed the possibility of Ukraine producing anti-ballistic Patriot interceptors.

Zelenskyy said he had a "good meeting" with Trump and said the US president "accepted that he will give us (Patriot) licenses".

Throughout the war, Ukraine has developed ways to defend itself against Russian drones and missiles, but super-fast ballistic missiles remain a challenge.

Of more than 120 ballistic missiles fired by Russia this month, Ukraine has downed less than a third of them, according to data from the Ukrainian air force.

title.en: US launches 'powerful' strikes on Iran after Trump threat to 'hit them hard'
title.zh: 美国在特朗普威胁‘重击’伊朗后发动‘强大’袭击

summary.en: The United States has launched powerful strikes against Iran, following an earlier threat from former President Trump to retaliate forcefully. This action signals an end to a brief period of calm, with concerns that more countries in the region will become involved in the ongoing conflict.
summary.zh: 在前总统特朗普威胁要“重击”伊朗之后，美国对伊朗发动了“强大”袭击。此举标志着短暂的停火结束，人们担心该地区会有更多国家卷入这场冲突。

body.en:
The United States military launched "powerful" strikes on Iran on Thursday, in retaliation for Tehran's attacks targeting US bases in Jordan as the Middle East war reignited and again drew in the Islamic republic's proxies.

The first strikes after a nearly week-long lull in fighting dashed hopes of a return to negotiations.

"The strikes are a powerful response to yesterday's attempted Iranian attacks on US forces based in the Middle East", US Central Command said.

On Wednesday, Saudi Arabia and the US announced strikes on militant bases in Iraq , while US ally Israel accused Iran-backed Hezbollah of a truce violation.

For two days, the world's biggest oil exporter, Saudi Arabia, has reported drone attacks targeting crude facilities that it blamed on Iraqi armed groups allied with Iran.

Iran meanwhile launched missiles at US ally Jordan, with Iranian state media later reporting a US attack near its border with Iraq.

"We'll be hitting them hard. They're going to get a beating," Trump told Fox News' correspondent before strikes, swearing for emphasis: "We are going to beat the 'effing s' out of them."

Saudi security analyst and researcher Hesham Alghannam told the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency: "Tehran is now using its proxy network to sustain leverage while the diplomatic track absorbs international attention."

Iran's state television, meanwhile, reported a US strike in the Piranshahr border area, after the Fars news agency quoted an official in West Azerbaijan province as saying a missile hit an uninhabited area, leaving no casualties.

Earlier, Jordan's army said it had intercepted five Iranian missiles, with Iran's Revolutionary Guards saying they had targeted US bases there.

"As long as the threats against the Islamic Republic of Iran continue ... the resistance will continue," they added.

On another front, US ally Israel accused Hezbollah of firing a drone overnight at an Israeli vehicle inside Lebanon, in what the military called "a blatant violation of the ceasefire".

Israel fought alongside the US in the first weeks of war against Iran, while battling Hezbollah in Lebanon, but it has yet to join the latest round of strikes.

In Iraq, a joint US-Saudi air operation followed attacks by what Saudi Arabia called "terrorist militias loyal to Iran" on its oil facilities.

The US military said logistics and weapons sites belonging to an Iran-aligned group were targeted in the strikes.

According to Iraq's Hashed al-Shaabi alliance, the attacks killed at least 20 of its members across seven provinces, including Baghdad.

title.en: How well are LGBTQ+ rights protected across Europe?
title.zh: 欧洲LGBTQ+权利保护状况如何？

summary.en: After an attack on Berlin's Pride event, the discussion has turned to the safety and legal protections for the LGBTQ+ community across Europe. The news examines the varying degrees to which queer rights are safeguarded in different European nations.
summary.zh: 柏林骄傲游行活动遭遇袭击后，德国LGBTQ+群体的境况成为讨论焦点。这篇报道审视了欧洲其他国家对酷儿权利的保护程度。

body.en:
After the attack on Berlin’s Pride event on Saturday, the situation of the LGBTQ+ community in Germany is a topic of conversation. How well are queer rights protected in other European countries? An overview.

Germany is still reeling from the weekend's car attack on its Berlin Pride celebration . Politicians are deep in discussion over which consequences the country should draw.

The center-left Social Democrats ( SPD ) are now mounting another effort to have LGBTQ+ rights enshrined in the German constitution , known as the Basic Law. Article 3 of the Basic Law addresses equality before the law, and currently states that, "no person shall be favored or disfavored because of sex, parentage, race, language, homeland and origin, faith or religious or political opinions. No person shall be disfavored because of disability." 

But no mention is made of gender identity or sexual orientation. The SPD wants to change that. 

Germany still has areas in which queer people — that is, individuals who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, intersex, asexual, non-binary, pangender and otherwise — are not yet fully equal under the law. In addition to the lack of constitutional protection, parentage law is a concern as well.

When a heterosexual couple has a child, the biological mother and her husband are automatically recognized as the child's legal parents. (When a heterosexual couple is unmarried, the biological father must submit a formal declaration to the youth welfare office to recognize his paternity to legally be considered the child's father.)

In queer family constellations, however, the legal situation is far more complex and often requires lengthy legal proceedings to establish parentage. Surrogacy , meanwhile, is illegal in German — a position the ruling conservative Christian Democratic ( CDU ) party has held for years . Despite having defended this position in the past, high-ranking CDU politician Jens Spahn recently disclosed he had sidestepped this ban and that he and his husband received a child via surrogacy in the US. He was pressured to resign from his position as parliamentary group leader as a result.

Hate crimes and violent attacks on queer people have increased, and many continue to report discrimination in their daily lives. But compared with other European nations, Germany still ranks relatively highly in terms of legal equality for queer people.

In a cross-comparison of 49 European countries, the International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association (ILGA), a global umbrella organization for LGBTQ+ advocacy groups, ranks Germany seventh in terms of protection and equality for queer residents. Spain holds first place, while Russia  comes in last...
body.zh: 周六柏林骄傲活动遇袭后，德国 LGBTQ+ 群体的处境成为人们谈论的话题。其他欧洲国家对酷儿权利的保护情况如何？概述。 德国仍在为周末柏林骄傲节庆祝活动中发生的汽车袭击事件而震惊。政治家们正在深入讨论该国应该承担哪些后果。 中左翼社会民主党 (SPD) 现在正在发起另一项努力，将 LGBTQ+ 权利写入德国宪法，即《基本法》。 《基本法》第三条规定法律面前人人平等，目前规定：“任何人不得因性别、出身、种族、语言、祖国和出身、信仰、宗教或政治见解而受到偏待或不偏待。任何人不得因残疾而受到偏待。” 但没有提及性别认同或性取向。社民党希望改变这一现状。 德国仍然有一些地区的酷儿群体——即那些被认为是女同性恋、男同性恋、双性恋、跨性别者、双性人、无性恋、非二元性别、跨性别者等的人——在法律上尚未完全平等。除了缺乏宪法保护外，亲子法也是一个问题。 当异性夫妇生育孩子时，生母及其丈夫自动被视为孩子的合法父母。 （当异性恋夫妇未婚时，生父必须向青少年福利办公室提交正式声明，承认其父子关系，才能在法律上被视为孩子的父亲。） 然而，在酷儿家庭中，法律情况要复杂得多，通常需要漫长的法律程序才能确定亲子关系。与此同时，代孕在德国是非法的——执政的保守基督教民主党（CDU）多年来一直坚持这一立场。尽管过去曾捍卫过这一立场，基民盟高级政治家詹斯·斯潘最近透露，他已经规避了这一禁令，并且他和丈夫在美国通过代孕生下了一个孩子。他因此被迫辞去议会党团领袖的职务。 针对酷儿人群的仇恨犯罪和暴力袭击有所增加，许多人继续报告在日常生活中受到歧视。但与其他欧洲国家相比，德国在酷儿法律平等方面仍然排名较高。 在对 49 个欧洲国家进行的交叉比较中，LGBTQ+ 倡导团体的全球伞式组织国际男女同性恋、双性恋、跨性别者和双性人协会 (ILGA) 在对酷儿居民的保护和平等方面将德国排名第七。西班牙位居第一，俄罗斯垫底……

Yahweh's word calls us to speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves and to defend the rights of all who are vulnerable. This reminds us of our responsibility to advocate for justice and...
reflection.zh: 近期对骄傲游行活动的袭击，凸显了许多LGBTQ+群体成员所面临的持续脆弱性，引发了对其法律保护的疑问。雅伟的话语呼召我们为不能发声的人说话，并捍卫所有弱势群体的权利。这提醒我们有责任为每个人的正义和安全发声，尤其当他们的尊严和保障受到威胁时。

title.en: Iran war: Egypt's difficult balancing act
title.zh: 伊朗战争：埃及艰难的平衡之举

summary.en: Egypt faces economic hardship due to the US-Iran war and new threats from Yemen's Houthi group, while simultaneously attempting to maintain good relations with all involved parties.
summary.zh: 美国与伊朗的战争已对埃及经济造成负面影响。现在，也门胡塞组织的新威胁可能使其情况恶化。与此同时，埃及正努力与所有各方保持良好关系。

body.en:
The US-Iran war has already had a negative economic impact on Egypt. Now new threats from the Houthi group in Yemen are likely to worsen that. At the same time, Egypt is trying to stay on good terms with all parties.

The Suez Canal boasts an array of impressive statistics. At 193 kilometers (120 miles) long, the Egyptian waterway is located between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and it saves ships traveling between Europe and Asia approximately 10,700 kilometers. This is why, since it was opened in 1869, the canal has become one of the world's most important trade routes.

However unrest in the Middle East has seen shipping companies increasingly avoid the Suez Canal over the past couple of years. The Houthi rebel group in Yemen has targeted shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, off the coast of Yemen. To get to the Suez Canal, ships must pass the Bab el-Mandeb and the Yemeni coast.

Recently the Houthis have again threatened to block ships passing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and there are fears that the trend to avoid the Suez Canal will accelerate. 

This is a huge problem for Egypt . Fees paid by shipping companies transiting the Suez Canal are an important source of revenue for the country.

According to Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi, Egypt likely lost around $7 billion (€6.15 billion) from a decrease in traffic through the Suez Canal in 2024 alone. The Reuters news agency said that at times, losses could have been as much as $8 million (€7 million) in a month.

This is why the economic consequence of that loss extends well beyond shipping. Egypt has not been impacted by the Iran conflict in a major military way, but it is certainly seeing an economic effect.

"Economically, Egypt is in a very ambivalent situation," says Stefan Lukas, director of German think tank Middle East Minds.

During 2025 and 2026, revenues from canal transits actually went up again, mainly because oil from the Gulf states was transported via Saudi pipelines to the Red Sea and then onwards through the Suez Canal. This was to avoid the Strait of Hormuz, which is being blocked by Iran and the US in turns. But the new threats by the Houthis to block the Bab el-Mandeb Strait could interfere with this alternative route.

It's bad timing for Egypt: Rising energy prices and the International Monetary Fund's reforms are already putting tough limits on Cairo's financial flexibility.

"Higher energy prices have made imports more expensive and driven up inflation," says Hanna Voss, an expert on the region with Germany's Friedrich Ebert Foundation. "The uncertainty in the Red Sea and potential disruptions to the passage through Bab el-Mandeb are jeopardizing Suez Canal revenues."

body.zh: 美伊战争已经对埃及经济产生了负面影响。现在，来自也门胡塞组织的新威胁可能会使情况变得更糟。与此同时，埃及正努力与各方保持良好关系。 苏伊士运河拥有一系列令人印象深刻的统计数据。埃及水道长 193 公里（120 英里），位于地中海和红海之间，往返于欧洲和亚洲之间的船舶可节省约 10,700 公里。这就是为什么自 1869 年开通以来，这条运河已成为世界上最重要的贸易路线之一。 然而，由于中东的动荡，过去几年航运公司越来越多地避开苏伊士运河。也门胡塞叛乱组织瞄准了也门沿海曼德海峡的航运。要到达苏伊士运河，船只必须经过曼德海峡和也门海岸。 近期胡塞武装再次威胁封锁曼德海峡船只，有人担心避开苏伊士运河的趋势将加速。 这对埃及来说是一个巨大的问题。通过苏伊士运河的航运公司支付的费用是该国的重要收入来源。 据埃及总统阿卜杜勒-法塔赫·塞西称，仅 2024 年，埃及就可能因苏伊士运河交通量减少而损失约 70 亿美元（61.5 亿欧元）。路透社称，有时一个月内的损失可能高达 800 万美元（700 万欧元）。 这就是为什么这种损失的经济后果远远超出了航运范围。 埃及并未受到伊朗冲突的重大军事影响，但它肯定看到了经济影响。 德国智库中东思想中心主任斯特凡·卢卡斯表示：“从经济角度来看，埃及的处境非常矛盾。” 2025年和2026年期间，运河过境收入实际上再次增加，主要是因为海湾国家的石油通过沙特管道运输到红海，然后通过苏伊士运河继续运输。这是为了避开被伊朗和美国轮番封锁的霍尔木兹海峡。但胡塞武装威胁封锁曼德海峡，可能会干扰这条替代路线。 对埃及来说，时机不佳：能源价格上涨和国际货币基金组织的改革已经对开罗的金融灵活性施加了严格的限制。 德国弗里德里希·艾伯特基金会的该地区专家汉娜·沃斯表示：“能源价格上涨使得进口产品更加昂贵，并推高了通货膨胀。” “红海的不确定性以及曼德海峡通道的潜在中断正在危及苏伊士运河的收入。” 埃及旅游业、资本流入和汇率……

The biblical call to "live at peace with everyone, as far as it depends on you," acknowledges the complexities of such a balancing act. In a world of escalating tensions, striving for harmony, even when difficult, remains a vital...

summary.en: Former US top health official Dr. Anthony Fauci's diaries reveal his dismissal of journalist Sharri Markson's COVID-19 origin investigation as 'nonsense.' Fauci, who was subpoenaed to appear at a Senate hearing on the virus, stated that Markson's reporting 'does not make any sense.'
summary.zh: 美国前首席卫生官员安东尼·福奇的日记显示，他驳斥记者沙里·马克森对新冠病毒起源的调查为“胡说八道”。福奇曾被传唤出席参议院关于该病毒的听证会，他表示马克森的报道“毫无道理”。

body.en: US former top health official, who was subpoenaed to appear at a Senate hearing into Covid-19, says Markson’s reporting about virus’s origin ‘does not make any sense’ Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Dr Anthony Fauci , the US’s chief medical adviser at the start of the pandemic, has described a book by News Corp investigative journalist Sharri Markson backing the “lab leak” theory of Covid-19’s origins as a “bunch of nonsense” in his newly released diaries. This week, Fauci, 85, was subpoenaed by the Republican senator Rand Paul to appear at a Senate hearing into Covid-19 and his handling of the pandemic. Continue reading...
body.zh: 被传唤出席参议院关于 Covid-19 的听证会的美国前高级卫生官员表示，马克森关于病毒起源的报道“没有任何意义”。 大流行开始时，美国首席医疗顾问安东尼·福奇博士将新闻集团调查记者莎莉·马克森 (Sharri Markson) 的一本支持 Covid-19 起源“实验室泄露”理论的书描述为在他新发表的日记中，“一堆废话”。本周，85 岁的福奇接到共和党参议员兰德·保罗的传票，出席参议院关于 Covid-19 及其处理疫情的听证会。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In public discourse, especially when complex issues like a pandemic's origins are debated, it is wise to consider all perspectives. As Proverbs 18:17 reminds us, the first account often seems right until another view is presented and examined. This encourages us to seek understanding from various sources before forming conclusions.
reflection.zh: 在公共讨论中，尤其当涉及疫情起源等复杂议题时，倾听各方观点是明智之举。正如箴言18:17提醒我们，先陈述案情的人似乎有理，直到另一方前来查问。这鼓励我们在下结论之前，从不同来源寻求理解。

verse.textEn: In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right, until someone comes forward and cross-examines.
verse.textZh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理；但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

title.en: The Chinese robot army transforming the UK's retail industry
title.zh: 改变英国零售业的中国机器人大军

summary.en: Britain's retail sector is increasingly adopting robotics from Chinese firms to combat low productivity and labor shortages.
summary.zh: 英国零售业正日益采用中国机器人公司的技术，以应对生产力低下和劳动力短缺的问题。

body.en:
Every time you click "buy" on an online order, the chances are that your purchase starts getting processed within minutes.

Increasingly, the journey starts with a squat silver floor robot gliding beneath a storage rack, lifting a shelf and carrying it across a warehouse to a waiting worker.

At Geek+'s factory in the eastern Chinese city of Hefei, which the BBC visited, fleets of the robots are built and tested before being shipped to warehouses around the world.

Some of Britain's biggest retailers - including Tesco, Asda and Next - now use the company's technology.

By automating these repetitive journeys, Geek+ says retailers can increase picking speeds, store more goods in spaces that are hard to reach for humans, and reduce errors.

Unlike traditional warehouse automation, which relies on fixed conveyor systems and permanent infrastructure, autonomous mobile robots can be deployed simply using QR code floor markers and safety fencing.

Geek+, which listed in Hong Kong last year in one of the biggest robotics share sales of 2025, has become the world's largest supplier of autonomous mobile robots.

The UK has struggled with weak productivity growth for more than a decade, and economists say wider adoption of robotics will be essential if businesses are to become more efficient.

In its 2026 report SME Technology Adoption in the United Kingdom, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) said technologies like robotics would be key to improving productivity.

According to the OECD, Britain's low adoption of robotics is "surprising" given its manufacturing heritage, noting that while UK firms have embraced mature digital technologies, they lag behind in robotics and automation.

That presents an opportunity for companies such as Geek+. The UK has one of Europe's largest e-commerce and logistics sectors, but many warehouses are still in the early stages of automation.

Britain has already become Geek+'s biggest European market, with UK partner MotionTech deploying more than 2,000 robots across 10 warehouse sites.

"Customers want fast deployable solutions," says Barry Pemberton, Account Director at MotionTech. "They want high volume, high storage, fast picking... ultimately on a smaller footprint with a reduced headcount."

"We seem to have a very big shortage of labour in the UK at the moment. These technologies are really important to keep businesses thriving and meet demand."

The Trades Union Congress (TUC), which represents almost 6 million UK workers, says robotics should be used to raise productivity and improve jobs, rather than simply cut labour costs.

body.zh: 每次您在在线订单上点击“购买”时，您的购买很可能会在几分钟内开始处理。 越来越多的旅程开始于一个矮胖的银色地板机器人在存储架下滑行，举起一个架子并将其穿过仓库交给等待的工人。 BBC 参观了 Geek+ 位于中国东部城市合肥的工厂，机器人车队在被运往世界各地的仓库之前进行了建造和测试。 英国一些最大的零售商——包括Tesco、Asda和Next——现在都在使用该公司的技术。 Geek+ 表示，通过自动化这些重复的旅程，零售商可以提高拣选速度，在人类难以到达的空间中存储更多商品，并减少错误。 与依赖固定输送系统和永久性基础设施的传统仓库自动化不同，自主移动机器人只需使用二维码地板标记和安全围栏即可部署。 Geek+去年在香港上市，成为2025年机器人股销量最大的公司之一，现已成为全球最大的自主移动机器人供应商。 十多年来，英国一直在与生产率增长疲软作斗争，经济学家表示，如果企业要提高效率，更广泛地采用机器人技术至关重要。 经济合作与发展组织 (OECD) 在其 2026 年英国中小企业技术采用报告中表示，机器人等技术将是提高生产力的关键。 经合组织表示，鉴于其制造业传统，英国机器人技术的采用率较低“令人惊讶”，并指出虽然英国公司已经采用了成熟的数字技术，但它们在机器人技术和自动化方面仍然落后。 这为 Geek+ 等公司提供了机会。英国拥有欧洲最大的电子商务和物流行业之一，但许多仓库仍处于自动化的早期阶段。 英国已经成为 Geek+ 最大的欧洲市场，英国合作伙伴 MotionTech 在 10 个仓库站点部署了 2000 多台机器人。 “客户需要快速部署的解决方案，”MotionTech 客户总监 Barry Pemberton 说道。 “他们想要高产量、高存储量、快速拣选……最终以更小的占地面积和更少的人员数量。” “目前英国的劳动力似乎非常短缺。这些技术对于保持企业繁荣和满足需求非常重要。” 代表近 600 万英国工人的工会大会 (TUC) 表示，机器人技术应该用于提高生产力和改善就业，而不是简单地削减劳动力成本。 在回应政府关于新的人工智能和创新战略的咨询时，它敦促部长们确保工人参与有关自动化的决策......

reflection.en: As robotics transform industries and redefine human roles, we are invited to consider the deeper purpose of our work. Colossians 3:23 reminds us to approach every task with diligence and integrity, working heartily as for Yahweh. This perspective elevates our labor beyond mere economic output, imbuing it with lasting meaning and dignity.
reflection.zh: 随着机器人技术改变行业并重新定义人类的角色，我们被邀请思考我们工作的更深层目的。歌罗西书3:23提醒我们，要以勤奋和正直的态度对待每一项任务，如同为雅伟而做。这种视角将我们的劳动提升到超越单纯经济产出的层面，赋予其持久的意义和尊严。

title.en: US bans Chinese and foreign-made humanoid robots
title.zh: 美国禁止中国及外国制造的仿人机器人

summary.en: The Trump administration has prohibited the import of humanoid and quadruped robots manufactured outside the United States, citing national security concerns. This ban could potentially escalate diplomatic tensions with China.
summary.zh: 特朗普政府以国家安全为由，禁止进口美国以外制造的仿人机器人和四足机器人。这项禁令可能会加剧与中国的外交紧张关系。

body.en:
The Trump administration has banned the import of humanoid and quadruped robots manufactured outside the United States, citing national security concerns. The ban could strain diplomatic tensions with China.

The United States has announced a ban on the import of foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots in a move which will likely exclude Chinese manufacturers from the US market and could strain tensions between Washington and Beijing .

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Tuesday that "advanced robotic devices" produced abroad posed national and cyber security risks to the United States.

The decision was based on findings from a White House task force which concluded that foreign-built robots could create "a cybersecurity risk that threatens the security of critical infrastructure" and "the safety and security" of US residents.

The FCC defines the relevant mobile robots as devices weighing more than two kilograms that use sensors, network connectivity and software to achieve autonomous navigation, including the avoidance of obstacles.

The market for humanoid and quadruped (also known as four-legged "robot dogs") is seen as a major international growth area, with US and Chinese companies competing to develop the technology.

And China has a clear lead, with analysts at Barclays estimating that Chinese-made humanoid robots account for around 85% of the global market share. Morgan Stanley experts predict that China's humanoid robot market could be worth $15 billion (€13.2 billion) by 2030.

"Chinese manufacturers have been scaling production and reducing costs faster than most overseas competitors," Morningstar analyst Kangyuxiao Li told the Associated Press .

In the US, firms such as Figure AI are already deploying humanoid robots on production lines, while tech giant Tesla plans to begin production of its "Optimus" robot this year.

Currently, however, US robot exports remain in their hundreds while Unitree and AGIBOT, two of China's biggest advanced robotics companies, each shipped more than 5,000 humanoid robots in 2025 alone, according to the technology research and advisory group Omdia.

FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the ban was also aimed at "secur[ing] America's critical supply chains."

But Li said the measures would not "materially slow China's overall humanoid development, given the size of its domestic manufacturing base and opportunities in other export markets."

Beyond the industrial market effects, the FCC ban could also have diplomatic consequences ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese Premier Xi Jinping in September.

body.zh: 特朗普政府以国家安全为由，禁止进口在美国境外制造的人形和四足机器人。该禁令可能会加剧与中国的外交紧张关系。 美国已宣布禁止进口外国制造的人形和四足机器人，此举可能会将中国制造商排除在美国市场之外，并可能加剧华盛顿和北京之间的紧张关系。 美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）周二表示，国外生产的“先进机器人设备”对美国构成国家和网络安全风险。 该决定是基于白宫特别工作组的调查结果，该工作组得出的结论是，外国制造的机器人可能会造成“威胁关键基础设施安全的网络安全风险”和美国居民的“安全保障”。 FCC将相关移动机器人定义为重量超过两公斤、使用传感器、网络连接和软件实现自主导航，包括避开障碍物的设备。 人形和四足动物（也称为四足“机器狗”）市场被视为主要的国际增长领域，美国和中国公司竞相开发该技术。 中国明显领先，巴克莱分析师估计，中国制造的人形机器人约占全球市场份额的 85%。摩根士丹利专家预测，到 2030 年，中国的仿人机器人市场价值可能达到 150 亿美元（132 亿欧元）。 晨星公司分析师李康宇告诉美联社：“中国制造商扩大生产和降低成本的速度比大多数海外竞争对手更快。” 在美国，Figure AI 等公司已经在生产线上部署人形机器人，而科技巨头特斯拉计划今年开始生产其“Optimus”机器人。 然而，根据技术研究和咨询集团 Omdia 的数据，目前美国机器人出口量仍为数百台，而中国最大的两家先进机器人公司 Unitree 和 AGIBOT 仅在 2025 年就分别出货了 5,000 多台人形机器人。 FCC 主席布伦丹·卡尔表示，该禁令还旨在“保护美国关键供应链的安全”。 但李表示，鉴于其国内制造基地的规模和其他出口市场的机会，这些措施不会“实质性地减缓中国整体人形机器人的发展”。 除了工业市场影响之外，FCC 禁令还可能在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普与中国总理习近平 9 月会晤之前产生外交后果。 美国已经禁止进口中国制造的无人机，并正在考虑限制中国开源人工智能（AI）模型，理由是……

title.en: Where Australia sits in this $6 billion race for influence as China's strategy shifts
title.zh: 澳大利亚在这场60亿美元的影响力竞争中处于何种位置，中国战略正在转变

summary.en: A new report indicates that China's strategic influence in the Pacific region, which was once significant, has recently diminished. This shift is noted amidst a broader competition for influence involving countries like Australia.
summary.zh: 一份新报告指出，中国在太平洋地区曾拥有的“真正立足点”已有所缩小。这一变化是在澳大利亚等国更广泛的地区影响力竞争中被观察到的。

body.en:
Australia has continued to outrank China as the Pacific's biggest source of development aid, contributing a third of loans and infrastructure investment to the region, according to a new report.

Looking at development projects across the Pacific between 2008 and 2024, the Lowy Institute report found that, after years of decline, aid to the region increased by 10 per cent in 2024.

Total development aid stood at US$4.1 billion ($5.85 billion) in that year, but the report's authors estimate that would drop to US$3.8 billion ($5.42 billion) in yet-to-be-released 2025 figures.

With China now shifting strategy from big debt-fuelled loans to smaller strategic aid, and amid major economic shocks in the Pacific, the contest for regional influence is coming under greater strain.

Australia was the Pacific's biggest donor in 2024, giving $2.14 billion in aid, which made up 37 per cent of all finance to the region in that year.

A total of $6 billion in financing was dispensed from New Zealand, China, and regional development banks.

Australia has also inked $3.4 billion in loan deals, ending China's reign as the region's leading lender.

"That's a product of many years of Australia pushing into these spaces, but it's meant that what was once a real foothold for China in the region has been narrowed," the report's lead author Riley Duke told SBS News.

"Australia is consistently providing the most grant financing to the region, and that picture hasn't really changed."

The report, released on Tuesday, says demand for Chinese loans has dropped since 2019 due to concerns about servicing the debt, more competition between lenders and Chinese banks' capital availability.

Australia is also a major financier of climate change mitigation projects in the Pacific, including a solar and battery storage facility for Palau to help generate 20 per cent of its electricity, and Tonga's Renewable Energy Stabilisation Package.

The fruits of those efforts have paid off for Australia, with a flurry of regional security deals announced in recent months, including with Fiji, Vanuatu , Papua New Guinea and Tuvalu.

"They are a clear marker of Australia establishing itself as the lead partner to the region," Duke said.

"Those deals ... take a long time to progress. They're complicated, but they reflect Australia establishing itself as an inalienably important partner to Pacific countries."

Developing Pacific Island nations have been hit hard by multiple shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic and more recently, fuel supply shortages caused by the United States-Israeli war on Iran.

summary.en: New research indicates that noise pollution, particularly from traffic, has serious health repercussions, including a link to Parkinson's disease, affecting sleep and overall well-being.
summary.zh: 新研究表明，噪音污染，特别是交通噪音，对健康造成严重影响，包括与帕金森病相关联，从而影响睡眠和整体福祉。

body.en: New research linking the issue to Parkinson’s disease adds to the evidence of serious health repercussions from traffic volume and other sources The roar of late-night traffic is not just annoying for those trying to sleep. It can also have profound effects on their health. A pioneering new study, published this month, has found a clear link between road noise and Parkinson’s disease. The research, which followed more than 3 million Danish participants, found a modest but consistent effect: for every 11.5dB rise in noise level, the risk of the degenerative disorder rose by 3% over the 18-year study. The study adds to the growing body of evidence that auditory nuisance is associated with serious physical consequences. The European Environment Agency reported last year that more than 110 million people across the continent suffer high levels of health-damaging noise pollution, with physiological stress and sleep disturbance leading to 66,000 early deaths annually as well as heart disease, diabetes and depression. It found that the harm caused was greater than from secondhand tobacco smoke exposure. Continue reading...
body.zh: 将这一问题与帕金森病联系起来的新研究进一步证明了交通流量和其他来源对健康造成的严重影响深夜交通的轰鸣声不仅仅让那些想睡觉的人感到烦恼。它还会对他们的健康产生深远的影响。本月发表的一项开创性的新研究发现，道路噪音与帕金森病之间存在明显的联系。这项研究跟踪了超过 300 万丹麦参与者，发现了一个适度但一致的效果：在 18 年的研究中，噪音水平每上升 11.5 分贝，退行性疾病的风险就会增加 3%。这项研究进一步证明听觉困扰与严重的身体后果有关。欧洲环境署去年报告称，欧洲大陆有超过 1.1 亿人遭受严重损害健康的噪音污染，生理压力和睡眠障碍每年导致 66,000 人过早死亡，以及心脏病、糖尿病和抑郁症。研究发现，造成的危害比接触二手烟草烟雾造成的危害更大。您对本文提出的问题有什么看法吗？如果您想通过电子邮件提交最多 300 字的回复，以便考虑在我们的信件部分发布，请单击此处。继续阅读...

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

summary.en: Australia has dropped to below pre-pandemic levels on a key social measure.

body.en:
Australia celebrates the value of mateship, but distrust between the population has grown to the highest level reported this decade.

A survey of over 3,500 people, conducted by the Australian National University in June, suggests Australians trust each other less than they did during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Professor Nicholas Biddle, head of ANU's School of Politics and International Relations, said some of the findings were concerning.

"Worryingly, interpersonal trust among Australians has fallen to 5.32 on a scale of 0 to 10 — the lowest value recorded in ANUpoll during the 2020s,'' he said.

"This sits below the pre-COVID value of 5.53 recorded in October 2019 and reverses the increase in trust observed during the pandemic."

Researchers asked participants three questions: whether they believed most people could be trusted, whether someone would take advantage of them if given the chance, and whether people are generally helpful or selfish in their choices.

While the results for all three indicated declining trust, the most dramatic decrease was in belief that others can be trusted, Biddle said.

He also noted that trust remains strongest among "older Australians, degree holders and the employed".

The findings follow data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics’ General Social Survey from 2025 that found half of Australians felt others could be trusted — compared to 61 per cent in 2020.

Similarly, Scanlon Foundation Research Institute CEO Anthea Hancocks said the findings reflected those of her organisation.

"People who are employed each day or very often are going to a workplace where there are other people working towards a similar goal — and they're getting paid," she explained.

"That gives you a greater sense of self-worth that you may not necessarily have if you're unemployed."

She suggested that higher trust among older Australians may be related to her organisation's findings that this cohort had "a higher sense of belonging than any other age group".

"That's generally because they know the world in which they're living; they're quite comfortable with their circumstances," she said.

"They know what they are and have an understanding of what the future holds. Unlike young people, whose sense of belonging is way below average."

The ANUpoll also found that between March and June of 2026, life satisfaction in Australia plateaued at 6.22 out of 10.

Over the same period, the proportion of those who experienced difficult or very difficult levels of financial stress decreased slightly from 34.9 per cent in March to 33 per cent in June.

body.en:
Ashleigh Middleton has spent months campaigning to keep a drug that's holding her cancer at bay on Australian shelves.

Now she's won — but says the uncertainty surrounding long-term access hasn't gone away.

The 31-year-old breast cancer patient was shocked when it was announced in April that Zoladex — a monthly implant used to suppress hormones in women with hormone-positive breast cancer as well as a range of other conditions affecting women — would be pulled from the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) and no longer supplied through its usual distribution pathway from 1 November.

The decision, made by the drug's manufacturer, AstraZeneca, prompted concern among patients and clinicians who questioned how those who rely on the treatment would access an alternative and whether suitable substitutes would be available for all conditions the implant is used to treat.

Angered by the move and worried about the precedent it could set for other medications, Middleton started a change.org petition, calling on AstraZeneca to reverse the decision and urging the federal government and the Pharmaceutical Benefits Advisory Committee to secure PBS-listed alternatives.

The company now says it will provide the monthly implant free of charge to patients who have no suitable alternative, with no end date listed — a shift from its earlier plan to provide six months of free access while patients transitioned to other arrangements.

Asked whether AstraZeneca could guarantee the medication would remain available, a spokesperson told SBS News: "The Zoladex Continuity Program is not a time-bound program."

For Middleton, it's a win worth celebrating — but not one that has settled her nerves.

"It's a really, really good step in the right direction, but it's definitely not all the way there," she tells SBS News.

"But I think AstraZeneca have recognised it was probably a bad decision on their part, so at least putting a little something extra in there, saying it's indefinitely going to be available and that there's no cut-off time, I think is a positive," Middleton says.

Two weeks on from that announcement, with November fast approaching, those affected are left with a mix of celebration, confusion and ongoing concern about what access will look like in practice.

While many people may not have heard of Zoladex, its 3.6mg implant has become a lifeline for many of the patients who rely on it.

It's prescribed to suppress hormones in premenopausal women with hormone-positive breast cancer, helping reduce the risk of recurrence by suppressing ovarian hormone production.

title.en: What is Garma Festival? Australia's biggest Indigenous gathering returns for 2026
title.zh: 什么是加尔马节？澳大利亚最大的原住民聚会将于2026年回归

summary.en: The annual Garma Festival, Australia's largest Indigenous gathering, is set to return this weekend on Yolŋu Country, celebrating Indigenous culture.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚最大的原住民聚会——一年一度的加尔马节将于本周末在约尔古地区举行，庆祝原住民文化。

body.en:
Thousands of people will travel to north-east Arnhem Land this week as the Garma Festival returns to Yolŋu Country for four days of ceremony, culture and national conversation.

Held on Gumatj Country in the Northern Territory, Garma remains Australia's largest Indigenous cultural gathering .

This year marks more than a quarter of a century since it started as a small community gathering, and will run from 31 July until 3 August.

Each year it brings together Yolŋu Elders, artists, young people, political leaders, academics, business representatives and visitors from across the country.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It is a place where ancient ceremony sits alongside some of Australia's biggest conversations about First Nations policy.

This year, those discussions will unfold without Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, despite his commitment last year to attend every Garma while serving as prime minister.

Hosted by the Yothu Yindi Foundation since 1999, Garma was established to celebrate and strengthen Yolŋu culture while creating a place where Aboriginal knowledge, leadership and ideas could be shared with the broader Australian community.

The word Garma comes from Yolŋu Matha and refers to a meeting place where different ideas come together through a process of two-way learning.

That philosophy remains central to the festival today. While Garma is grounded in Yolŋu ceremony and tradition, it has also become one of Australia's most influential forums for discussion on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander affairs.

Each year, governments, community organisations, academics and industry leaders travel to Arnhem Land to listen, learn and engage directly with Yolŋu leaders on Country.

Garma is held at Gulkula, a sacred ceremonial site on Gumatj Country near Nhulunbuy in north-east Arnhem Land.

Surrounded by stringybark forest and overlooking the Gulf of Carpentaria, Gulkula has been a place of ceremony and renewal for generations.

According to Yolŋu tradition, it is where the ancestor Ganbulapula introduced the yidaki into Yolŋu life, making it one of the region's most culturally significant places.

Unlike many conferences, Garma is held on Yolŋu Country and led on Yolŋu terms.

Rather than Aboriginal leaders travelling to Canberra, governments, institutions and organisations travel to Arnhem Land, placing First Nations culture, knowledge and authority at the centre of the national conversation.

Visitors camp on Country throughout the four-day festival and are asked to observe cultural protocols guided by their Yolŋu hosts.

title.en: There's something else Neil the seal wrecked in Tasmania — the council's bank account
title.zh: 海豹尼尔在塔斯马尼亚还毁坏了一些东西——议会的银行账户

summary.en: The social media sensation, famous for loathing bollards, has returned to the ocean for another year.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Neil the seal captures hearts and global attention during his visits to Tasmania, but his most recent stay racked up a bill of more than $36,000.

The five-year-old elephant seal hauls out twice a year to rest and moult in the island state's south-east, where he was born.

His antics, including crushing bollards and fences, and lounging on quiet beach-side streets, have drawn millions of views on social media.

In June, wildlife authorities issued a blunt public statement, urging people to keep their distance or risk "loving Neil to death".

His 15-day stay at Seven Mile Beach cost the local Clarence City Council a total of $31,540.53 — the majority relating to staffing and labour.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

There is also a repair bill for one flattened street sign, 10 knocked-over bollards and one crushed fence, costing council $1,297.70 in materials.

Staff, including a 24-hour security presence, spent 275.5 hours managing traffic and crowds and repairing damage.

"Neil is a wild animal, and the overexposure and constant public attention he received could have led to a more dramatic outcome," Blomeley said.

"Wherever he decides to come ashore next, I hope he is given the space and time he needs."

Right-to-information documents obtained by the ABC show that Tasmania's natural resources and environment department has spent more than $45,000 managing Neil's four haul-outs in 2025 and 2026.

Neil's June haul-out cost the department $4,794, but it was still calculating the full price tag.

Neil, who currently weighs one tonne, safely returned to sea in early July and is expected to come back to Tasmania later in the year once he's done feeding in the Southern Ocean.

He was rescued by wildlife authorities after being born on a beach in southern Tasmania.

Experts have said his "jousting" with posts and other objects is natural behaviour, and something seals of his age usually do with each other.

There were once southern elephant seals in Tasmania, but they were wiped out by hunting in the early 1800s.

"Neil is potentially one of the first southern elephant seal pups to be born back in Tasmania," department wildlife expert Kris Carlyon has said.

"Regardless of the resource burden and the challenges that Neil throws, we're pleased to see him."

body.en:
Australia's second-largest telco is facing legal action over a major network failure that caused a widespread Triple Zero outage.

The Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA) alleges Optus breached two legal obligations more than 1,000 times during the outage on 18 September, 2025.

Access to emergency call services was essential to protect the public, the regulator's chair Nerida O'Loughlin said.

"Australians rightly expect that when they call Triple Zero, their call will connect," she said in a statement on Thursday.

"The circumstances of this outage meant that did not reliably occur, leaving people unable to connect to potentially life-saving services.

"Giving access to the emergency call service is not optional; it is a fundamental legal obligation, and the most important public safety responsibility telecommunications providers have."

Optus failed to give customers who made Triple Zero calls access to the emergency call service and to ensure those calls were carried appropriately , the regulator alleged.

The proceedings against the Singaporean-owned company announced on Thursday will be heard in the Federal Court.

The legal action follows the massive outage which went for almost 14 hours and impacted 600 calls, with 455 failing to connect.

An independent review, released by Optus in December, found there were at least 10 mistakes by the company and its contractor Nokia during an upgrade.

It took Optus and Nokia 13 hours to understand the problem, with an Optus call centre not escalating early concerns from five people who said their Triple Zero calls weren't working, the report by experienced executive Kerry Schott found.

The watchdog has previously taken action against the telco following another Triple Zero outage in November 2023.

The action resulted in Singtel Optus subsidiaries, including Optus Mobile, paying more than $12 million in infringement notice penalties for breaches relating to emergency calls.

"The recurrence of a major network outage affecting emergency calls so soon after the November 2023 outage is a significant concern and one of the reasons the ACMA has decided to take this matter to court," O'Loughlin said.

"The ACMA will not hesitate to take strong enforcement action where alleged telco failures have jeopardised public access to the critical emergency call service."

Optus acknowledged the Federal Court proceedings, adding it would be inappropriate to comment further.

"Our focus remains on building a stronger and better Optus," the company said in a statement to the Australian Associated Press.

Australia's eSafety Commissioner has announced legal action against messaging app Telegram for its failure to remove terrorist content, just one day after Russia charged the app's founder with aiding Ukrainian spies to co-ordinate domestic terrorist attacks.

eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant told reporters on Thursday that Telegram continued to host videos linked to the Christchurch mosque shootings and executions by the self-proclaimed Islamic State group, both illegal and restricted Class 1 content in Australia.

Grant said the app has "a fundamental responsibility to take reasonable steps to prevent the hosting, sharing and amplification of this harmful material".

Telegram, based in the United Arab Emirates, is one of the world's largest messaging platforms with more than one billion active users worldwide. It is not included in Australia's youth social media ban .

Grant said her agency first began compliance talks with the digital platform in March 2024. Despite Telegram's engagement, Grant said the platform continued to host harmful content.

"We allege that this content remained publicly accessible on the service long after Telegram had been put on notice by user reports," she said.

The maximum penalty for non-compliance is $54.4 million; however, Grant told the press that the appropriate penalty was a "matter for the court".

In 2025, Telegram was fined $957,780 by the eSafety Commissioner for delays in reporting the steps the platform has taken to minimise terrorism and child abuse material.

On Wednesday, Russia said it had charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activity, alleging the app was being used by Ukrainian spies to organise attacks inside Russia.

In response, Telegram's official account on X posted an image of the Russian-born billionaire making an obscene gesture with his middle finger.

The charges, announced by Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB), marked the culmination of a long investigation against Dubai-based Durov and Telegram.

Russia has effectively throttled the service as part of a wider campaign to cut off access to foreign tech platforms and tighten control over the internet.

Russians can now access Telegram only via a virtual private network to encrypt traffic and conceal their location. Yet state bodies including the Kremlin and the defence ministry continue to post to it daily.

The app has been described as a "virtual battlefield" in the war between Russia and Ukraine, where it is used by officials, soldiers and influential bloggers on both sides.

body.en:
From secret dossiers to "shake downs" and dodgy alleged donations, the first few days of the NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) investigation into the NSW Liberal Party have shone a light on factionalism and lobbying in state politics.

The hearings, which started in Sydney this week, centre on the alleged actions of a religious conservative faction of the NSW Liberal Party between 2019 and 2023.

The first few days of evidence have featured a cast of figures — from disgraced property developer Jean Nassif to the brother of former Liberal premier Dominic Perrottet.

Not even federal Opposition leader Angus Taylor could escape the net of the hearings, with his name appearing in messages alleging he was solicited for undisclosed donations — which Taylor denies, and he is not under investigation for.

It's not the first time the state's anti-corruption watchdog has investigated the actions of political parties, with ICAC ruling in 2023 that former Liberal premier Gladys Berejiklian engaged in "serious corrupt conduct" during her relationship with former MP Daryl Maguire.
